```{r setup}
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 13))
# inputs (not tracked): agent/nb07/collect.sh; master copy on /rsstu, see "Why"
d <- "gap_markers_dilution"
rd <- function(f, ...) fread(file.path(d, f), ...)
taxa <- c(Zd = "diploperennis", Zh = "huehuetenangensis", Zv = "parviglumis", Zx = "mexicana")
runs <- c(A = "alone", B = "+ parviglumis", C = "+ mexicana")
nil <- fread("../../meta/samples.csv")[, .(line = sample_id, nil_id)]
nil_label <- function(x) paste0(nil[match(x, line), nil_id], " (", x, ")")
lc <- rd("line_checks.tsv", na.strings = ".")
# one call set per taxon: run B for huehuetenangensis and parviglumis, 1270808 diploperennis, 1273053 mexicana
lc_taxa <- lc[run %in% c("B", "1270808", "1273053")][, taxon := taxa[substr(donor, 1, 2)]]
expected <- 12.5 # BC2 donor allele frequency, kept by selfing
```

## Why

Questions of the user, 2026-10-16, while the diploperennis partner runs D-F ran
(`docs/runs/genotype_diploperennis_partners_chr10.md`):

- gap markers skip the witness veto, so how can they smooth the genotypes of notebook 06;
- whether the smoothing erases diluted signal, and what that means for mapping;
- whether the low donor allele frequency is selection against the donor, as in TeoNAM.

Inputs (not in git): small tables in `gap_markers_dilution/`, made by `agent/nb07/collect.sh` (log there) from the runs
on hazel and from the measurement jobs 1332113 and 1332684; master copy in
`/rsstu/users/r/rrellan/BZea/ZEAL/genotype/notebook_inputs/gap_markers_dilution/`; copy it next to this notebook to
re-render. Lines are named by registry NIL id with the sample in parentheses.

## 1. Where the gap markers come from

A donor's RTIGER markers are the union sites gap filling called ALT for it (Milestone 9a): its own tier-A sites and gap
sites, discovered in other donors. Each gap marker, looked up in the donor's own discovery (CRISP, then the witness veto,
then the tiers):

```{r origin}
go <- rd("gap_origin.tsv")
go[, class := fifelse(grepl("^in discovery", class), "in discovery, tier B or C", class)]
knitr::kable(dcast(go[src == "gap", .(n = sum(n)), by = .(run, donor, markers, class)],
                   run + donor + markers ~ class, value.var = "n", fill = 0),
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
bc1 <- rd("gap_marker_bc1.tsv")
bc1[, tier_a_pct := round(100 * as.numeric(sub(".*'A': ([0-9]+).*", "\\1", tiers)) / markers_in_table, 1)]
knitr::kable(bc1[, .(run, donor, markers = src, `tier A at the union (%)` = tier_a_pct,
                     `BC1 reads` = median_bc1_reads, `BC1 ALT reads` = median_bc1_alt,
                     `pools with ALT` = median_pools_alt, LLR = median_LLR)],
             caption = "Medians over the markers; tier from the donor's BC1 pools counted at the union sites.")
```

Most gap markers are sites the donor's own CRISP never called (about 90 % for Zh.0020_P3, half for Zh.0030_P4); about 9
in 10 score tier A when the union is counted on the same BC1 reads (bcftools mpileup, MAPQ 20, base quality 20). So
gap filling mostly adds sites the BC1 pools support, not promoted tier-B sites. For Zh.0030_P4, 44 % were removed by
its witness veto: BC1 reads ALT, its lines do not.

## 2. Do the lines carry them

```{r lines}
gr <- rd("gap_marker_reads.tsv")
knitr::kable(gr[, .(run, donor, markers = src, n = markers, `with an ALT read in the lines (%)` = pct_alt_of_covered)],
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
gz <- rd("gap_marker_zero_alt.tsv")[k == 5]
knitr::kable(gz[, .(run, donor, markers = src, `>= 5 reads from lines in donor state` = markers_k,
                    `no ALT read (%)` = pct_zero_alt)],
             caption = "A marker read only REF where its lines are in a donor state: probably REF in the donor.")
gs <- rd("gap_marker_states.tsv")
gs[, state := factor(state, 0:2, c("REF", "HET", "ALT"))]
knitr::kable(dcast(gs[run == "B"], donor + src ~ state, value.var = "alt_pct"),
             caption = "Run B: ALT % of the lines' reads per segment state, own vs gap markers (run C within a point).")
```

- Fewer gap markers have an ALT read in the lines, but read depth there is low; inside donor segments, Zh.0020_P3's
  gap markers read ALT about as often as its own (HET 36 vs 41 %, ALT 77 vs 78 %).
- About 6 % of Zh.0020_P3's testable gap markers (3x its own markers' share) and a fifth of Zh.0030_P4's read no ALT:
  false alleles for this donor. Zh.0030_P4 carries almost no chr10 introgression (notebook 06), so its test is weak.
- In REF segments gap markers are cleaner: 0.4-1.4 % ALT against 2.6-2.9 % at own markers.

## 3. `r nil_label("PN9_SID806")`: what smoothing did

```{r paint, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 11}
seg <- rd("segments.tsv")[run %in% c("A", "B")]
snp <- rd("snp50k_chr10_zh0020.tsv")[line %in% seg$line]
src <- c(SNP50K = "NILs (RTIGER 50K)", A = "union alone (run A)", B = "+ parviglumis (run B)")
pt <- rbind(snp[, .(source = src["SNP50K"], line, start, end, state)],
            seg[, .(source = src[run], line, start, end, state)])
lines_ord <- rev(sort(unique(pt$line)))
pt[, row := match(line, lines_ord)]
pt[, source := factor(source, levels = src)]
pt[, state := factor(state, 0:2, c("REF", "HET", "ALT"))]
ggplot(pt) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = start / 1e6, xmax = end / 1e6, ymin = row - 0.48, ymax = row + 0.48, fill = state)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(REF = "gold", HET = "springgreen4", ALT = "purple4"), name = "State") +
  facet_grid(. ~ source) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = match("PN9_SID806", lines_ord), labels = nil_label("PN9_SID806"), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Zh.0020_P3, chr10 ancestry per BC2S3 sample", x = "chr10 position (Mb)", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r sid806, fig.height = 4}
iv <- rd("sid806_intervals.tsv")[A_reads >= 20]
ivl <- melt(iv[, .(mid = (start + end) / 2e6, A = A_alt_pct, `B own` = B_own_alt_pct, `B gap` = B_gap_alt_pct,
                   nA = A_reads, nBo = B_own_reads, nBg = B_gap_reads)],
            id.vars = c("mid", "nA", "nBo", "nBg"), variable.name = "markers", value.name = "alt_pct")
ggplot(ivl, aes(mid, alt_pct, colour = markers)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(2.6, 41), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(A = "grey30", `B own` = "purple4", `B gap` = "darkorange")) +
  labs(title = paste(nil_label("PN9_SID806"), ": intervals where runs A and B disagree"),
       x = "chr10 position (Mb)", y = "ALT % of the line's reads",
       caption = "Intervals with >= 20 reads in run A; dashed: own-marker REF noise (2.6 %) and HET (41 %).") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
knitr::kable(lc[line == "PN9_SID806", .(run = runs[run], segments = n_donor_segments, `REF % ALT` = ref_alt_pct,
                                        `HET % ALT` = het_alt_pct, `ALT % ALT` = alt_alt_pct)],
             caption = "Line checks of the sample.")
```

- Run A breaks 1.6-98 Mb into HET pieces; run B calls it REF. There the sample's own markers read 14-25 % ALT, far
  above REF noise and below HET: about 0.18 donor allele frequency (/ 0.82, notebook 05), about 2 of the 6 plants HET.
- Gap markers read half that or less, so they pulled the stretch to REF and the ALT segment at 143-146 Mb to HET.
- The diluted signal is not lost: run B's line checks fail the sample (REF 7.5 % ALT, 7 donor segments).

## 4. Diluted tissue pools across taxa

```{r refalt}
knitr::kable(lc_taxa[!is.na(ref_alt_pct), .(
  lines = .N, `median REF % ALT` = median(ref_alt_pct), `p90` = quantile(ref_alt_pct, 0.9),
  `lines > 3 %` = sum(ref_alt_pct > 3), `lines > 5 %` = sum(ref_alt_pct > 5),
  `segments, > 3 %` = as.numeric(median(n_donor_segments[ref_alt_pct > 3])),
  `segments, <= 3 %` = as.numeric(median(n_donor_segments[ref_alt_pct <= 3]))
), by = taxon], digits = 1)
ggplot(lc_taxa[!is.na(ref_alt_pct)], aes(ref_alt_pct, fill = taxon)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, boundary = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~taxon, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "ALT % of the reads in REF segments", y = "samples") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

7-15 % of the samples read more than 3 % ALT in their REF segments, and those also have more donor segments. Read
as pools of 6 plants where only some carry an authentic introgression (user, 2026-10-16), plus some low-depth noise.

## 5. The donor allele deficit

### Called and hidden

```{r dilution}
dl <- rd("dilution.tsv")
knitr::kable(dl[, .(taxon = taxa[taxon], run, donors, lines, `called (%)` = called_pct,
                    `hidden in REF segments (%)` = hidden_pct, `together (%)` = called_plus_hidden_pct,
                    `expected (%)` = expected_pct)],
             caption = "Donor allele frequency on chr10 (HET 0.5, ALT 1, by bp, mean over samples); hidden: REF % ALT above the taxon's median sample, / 0.82.")
```

Hiding diluted signal in REF segments costs about half a point; the deficit is 3-7 points.

### Against TeoNAM and SNP50K

```{r teonam}
tn <- rd("teonam_table1.tsv")[, teo_allele := teosinte_pct + het_pct / 2]
knitr::kable(tn, col.names = c("population", "RILs", "W22 %", "HET %", "teosinte %", "teosinte allele % (computed)"),
             caption = "Chen et al. (2019) Table 1, TeoNAM BC1S4 (expected 73.44 / 3.13 / 23.44 %, allele 25 %).")
st <- rd("snp50k_taxa.tsv")[set == "our chr10 lines"]
cmp <- rbind(
  data.table(set = "TeoNAM, 5 families, all chromosomes", calls = "per RIL", obs = tn[population == "Composite", teo_allele],
             exp = 25),
  dl[, .(set = paste0("ZEAL ", taxa[taxon], ", chr10"), calls = paste0("zealgt (", run, ")"),
         obs = called_plus_hidden_pct, exp = expected)],
  st[, .(set = paste0("ZEAL ", taxa[taxon], ", chr10 (", lines, " samples)"), calls = "SNP50K RTIGER",
         obs = chr10_pct, exp = expected)]
)
knitr::kable(cmp[, .(set, calls, `observed / expected` = sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", obs, exp), ratio = round(obs / exp, 2))])
```

The same direction as TeoNAM, where Chen et al. report "an excess of maize alleles" in all subpopulations; within a
call set the taxa compare, across call sets only the direction. SNP50K sits lower partly because it calls
donor-homozygous segments HET (notebook 06).

### Coverage, families and markers

```{r cov}
knitr::kable(rd("coverage.tsv")[, taxon := taxa[taxon]], caption = "Sample coverage and called chr10 donor allele frequency by coverage band.")
pd <- rd("per_donor.tsv")[, taxon := taxa[substr(donor, 1, 2)]][taxon %in% c("parviglumis", "mexicana", "diploperennis")]
ggplot(pd, aes(markers / 1e3, freq_pct, colour = taxon)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(x = "union-ALT markers on chr10 (thousands)", y = "donor allele frequency (%)",
       title = "Per family: chr10 donor allele frequency against its markers") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
knitr::kable(pd[, .(families = .N, `median (%)` = median(freq_pct), `mean (%)` = mean(freq_pct),
                    `under 2 %` = sum(freq_pct < 2), `median markers` = median(markers),
                    `median BC1 coverage` = median(bc1_mean_cov),
                    `Spearman freq ~ markers` = cor(freq_pct, markers, method = "spearman")), by = taxon], digits = 2)
```

Line coverage is the same for parviglumis and mexicana (0.42x and 0.40x), and neither markers nor BC1 coverage predict
a family's frequency. parviglumis is lower through its whole family distribution, not through families without chr10
introgression.

### Along the chromosome and across chromosomes

```{r windows, fig.height = 6}
cct <- data.table(chr = c("chr10", "chr9"), mb = c(96.18, 120.96), gene = c("ZmCCT10", "ZmCCT9"))
wl <- function(f, calls, chr) {
  w <- melt(rd(f), id.vars = "window_Mb", variable.name = "taxon", value.name = "freq")
  w[, `:=`(mb = as.numeric(sub("-.*", "", window_Mb)) + 2.5, taxon = taxa[sub("_pct", "", taxon)], calls = calls, chr = chr)]
}
w <- rbind(wl("windows_zealgt_chr10.tsv", "zealgt", "chr10"), wl("windows_snp50k_chr10.tsv", "SNP50K RTIGER", "chr10"),
           wl("windows_snp50k_chr9.tsv", "SNP50K RTIGER", "chr9"))
ggplot(w[taxon != "huehuetenangensis"], aes(mb, freq, colour = taxon)) +
  geom_vline(data = cct, aes(xintercept = mb), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(calls ~ chr, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "position (Mb, 5-Mb windows)", y = "donor allele frequency (%)",
       caption = "Dashed: ZmCCT10 (chr10 96.18 Mb) and ZmCCT9 (chr9 120.96 Mb), v5 (zealhmm candidate table).") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
sc <- rd("snp50k_chroms.tsv")
setnames(sc, c("chr", taxa[sub("_pct", "", names(sc)[-1])]))
knitr::kable(sc, caption = "SNP50K RTIGER donor allele frequency (%) per chromosome.")
```

- No parviglumis dip at ZmCCT10 or ZmCCT9; on chr10 it is lower along the whole chromosome.
- Across chromosomes parviglumis is higher than mexicana on chr4-8 and lower on chr1-3, 9, 10; equal over all ten
  (SNP50K 6.8 %).

### Tests of selection for the genome-wide genotypes

Planned, not run (2026-10-16). Each family (donor) is the unit: its samples share one donor gamete, and neighbouring
windows share segments. A BC2S3 sample is the selfed progeny of one BC2S2 plant, so its pool estimates that parent's
dosage, and its calls are read at the BC2S2 level (84.4 % REF, 6.25 % HET, 9.4 % donor homozygous; donor allele
12.5 %). The neutral null for every test is the zealtiger pedigree simulation (BC1 pools, BC2, selfings, real map,
each family's pool and sample numbers), which carries the founder effect.

1. **Transmission, BC1 to BC2S3.** Each donor segment in a BC1 plant has a Mendelian chance of reaching each descendant
   sample: observed vs expected transmission per segment, as a transmission test (TDT). A family is compared with its
   own ancestors, not with an external 12.5 %. Needs donor segments called in the BC1 pools.
2. **Parallel change across families** (evolve-and-resequence). Selection moves all families at a locus the same way,
   drift moves each on its own: per window, a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test across families (observed vs expected
   donor allele count). All taxa together for selection in the B73 background, one taxon for adaptation.
3. **More spread than drift allows** (Lewontin-Krakauer / F~ST~-outlier style). The variance of donor frequency
   across loci under drift alone is set by the pedigree (plants advanced per generation); loci far outside the
   simulated spread are candidates.
4. **Segment ends and lengths near a selected locus.** Selection for the donor allele keeps longer donor segments
   around it (hitchhiking); selection against it piles up recombination breakpoints nearby, with donor segments
   stopping short of it. From the RTIGER segments; less affected by dilution than frequencies.
5. **Gametophytic factors.** Maize x teosinte crosses carry gametophyte loci that bias transmission from
   heterozygotes (*Ga1* and *Tcb1* on chr4, *Ga2* on chr5): positive controls for distortion. Which taxa carry which
   alleles is to be checked in the literature.
6. **Association with fitness traits.** A QTL scan (family covariate) for seed set, germination, vigour or flowering
   time, if scored, for loci the breeding could have selected on.
7. **Generation by environment.** If generations alternated between the PV23 winter nursery (short days) and summer
   nurseries (long days), the photoperiod hypothesis predicts locus-specific changes that differ between
   environments. Needs the nursery history and more than one genotyped generation.
8. **HET to donor-homozygous ratio, per locus and genome-wide**, against BC2S2's 0.67 (6.25 / 9.375; earlier skim
   analyses about 2:1). With the allele frequency it separates selection against donor homozygotes (recessive
   deleterious alleles, as Chen et al. suggest near *tga1*: the ratio rises well above 0.67, the frequency falls less)
   from additive selection against the allele (HET and homozygous classes shrink together).
9. **Divergence between taxa.** Per-family donor allele frequency, parviglumis (40) vs mexicana (42), genome-wide and
   per chromosome; permutation of taxon labels across families, or a mixed model (sample frequency ~ taxon +
   (1 | family)).

Where the reading fails, and how it is guarded:

- **Diluted pools:** when the 6 sampled plants do not represent their sibship (`r nil_label("PN9_SID806")`), the
  pool does not measure the parent's dosage; the line checks flag them (REF % ALT > 3).
- **State calls:** HET called where the pool reads near-homozygous ALT inflates the ratio of test 8 (SNP50K:
  Zh.0020_P3 0.1 % donor homozygous against 6.8-7.1 % in the unions), so test 8 uses zealgt calls.
- **Detection bias:** detection that differs by taxon or region mimics selection. A caller calibration per taxon
  (simulated reads, known truth), including TIL01 reads (parviglumis mapping bias not measured), or comparisons
  within one call set and taxon. Test 1 is the least affected (BC1 and samples share the reference bias).
- **Data:** all tests need the genome-wide zealgt genotypes; tests 1 and 4 also need donor segments called in the
  BC1 pools.

## 6. Notes (2026-10-16)

- **Gap markers are mostly CRISP misses**, not promoted tier-B sites: per-donor CRISP leaves out sites its own BC1 reads
  score tier A at the union. One CRISP over all BC1 pools and every donor's witness pool would be the principled form
  (user); a separate test (`agent/diplo_chr10/joint_crisp_test_plan.md`).
- **For mapping, calling diluted stretches REF is preferred** (user): it puts the error in the large REF class. SNP50K
  RTIGER calls the same stretches REF: of the bp our runs call REF in samples with REF % ALT > 3, SNP50K calls
  96-99 % REF and 1-4 % HET (clean samples: 99.7-99.9 % REF; table below). Unlike SNP50K, which calls
  donor-homozygous segments HET, the union runs keep the classes separate (segment ALT % nearer 0 / 50 / 100). For
  choosing samples at a candidate gene the line checks flag the diluted ones (REF % ALT > 3), per sample, not per
  position: a windowed flag would be a design change.

```{r snp50k_in_ref}
sr <- rd("snp50k_in_ref.tsv")[, taxon := taxa[taxon]]
knitr::kable(sr, col.names = c("taxon", "samples", "group", "SNP50K REF (%)", "SNP50K HET (%)", "SNP50K ALT (%)"),
             caption = "SNP50K RTIGER states over the bp our runs call REF (run B, 1270808, 1273053; samples in both).")
```

- **Diluted pools are authentic introgressions carried by some of the 6 sampled plants** (user); 6 of the 12 planted
  plants estimate the bulk's allele frequency well. If the phenotype came from the same plants, their dose is
  fractional, and neither REF nor HET states it.
- **The donor allele deficit has the direction of TeoNAM's**; dilution explains half a point of 3-7. On chr10 neither
  a photoperiod-gene dip nor a consistent lowland (parviglumis) deficit across chromosomes is seen: the parviglumis
  chr10 shift is about 2.4 standard errors of the family mean and other chromosomes differ by 1-2 points in both
  directions. The genome-wide run decides.
- **Mexicana above parviglumis on chr10, in both call sets** (user, 2026-10-16): zealgt 9.3 vs 7.2 % (gap 2.1
  points), SNP50K on the same samples 6.3 vs 5.2 % (gap 1.1), mexicana higher in most 5-Mb windows from 10 to 110 Mb.
  Genome-wide SNP50K shows no difference (6.8 vs 6.8 %; the sign changes between chromosomes). Not yet known for
  zealgt genome-wide.
- **Tests, once zealgt genotypes cover the genome**: section 5, "Tests of selection for the genome-wide genotypes"
  (divergence between taxa, the overall deficit after a caller calibration per taxon, per-window distortion shared by
  all taxa or in one only, with Inv4m as the first check, zealhmm `analysis/zeal-inv4m-rtiger-genotype.qmd`).
